Day 1
From Hotel: 7 min · 3 min → Santa Monica Pier
1. Santa Monica Pier
Built in 1909 and extended in 1916, this municipal pier marks the western terminus of historic U.S. Route 66. It holds Pacific Park amusement park with a solar-powered Ferris wheel, a 1922 hippodrome carousel, and the Santa Monica Pier Aquarium below the deck.
Read more

~1 hr 30 min
Ocean Front Walk · Santa Monica Pier
3 min · 4 min → Santa Monica State Beach
2. Santa Monica State Beach
A 3.5-mile white-sand beach managed by Los Angeles County, stretching from the pier north toward Malibu. Facilities include a paved multi-use path, volleyball courts, lifeguard towers, and access to the 22-mile Marvin Braude Bike Trail running the length of Santa Monica Bay.
Read more
Open 24/7

10 min · 5 min → Third Street Promenade
3. Third Street Promenade
Three car-free blocks of outdoor retail, dining, and street performance in the heart of downtown Santa Monica, running between Broadway and Wilshire Boulevard. Anchored at the south end by Santa Monica Place; licensed street performers occupy designated zones throughout the corridor.

Day 2
From Hotel: 14 min · 3 min → California Heritage Museum
1. California Heritage Museum
A landmarked 1894 house — the "First Roy Jones House," moved to this site in 1977 and landmarked in 1979 — now home to a small museum with rotating exhibits on Southern California surf, skate, and Native American culture, including one guest-curated by original Z-Boy Nathan Pratt.

27 min · 5 min → Muscle Beach
2. Muscle Beach
An outdoor weightlifting platform on Ocean Front Walk that gave rise to American bodybuilding and fitness culture starting in the 1930s–60s — training ground of early greats before the scene shifted to Gold's Gym. Still a working public gym today, framed by the boardwalk's carnival atmosphere.
Read more

1 min · 2 min → Venice Beach Skatepark
3. Venice Beach Skatepark
A 16,000-square-foot oceanfront concrete skatepark opened in 2009 on the sand next to Muscle Beach, with a street plaza, snake run, and pool section — one of the most recognized skateparks in the world, built directly on Ocean Front Walk with the Pacific as a backdrop.
Read more

17 min · 5 min → Venice Canals Historic District
4. Venice Canals Historic District
Six remaining canals from Abbot Kinney's 1905 "Venice of America" development, restored in 1991–93 and now lined with architecturally eclectic waterfront homes, gondola-style footbridges, and resident ducks — a quiet, non-commercial curiosity a few blocks from the boardwalk.
Read more
Open 24/7
~45 min
Dell Ave & Eastern Ct · Venice
13 min → Bergamot Station Arts Center
5. Bergamot Station Arts Center
A former railroad depot — first used in 1875 as a stop on the Los Angeles and Independence Railroad — converted into a 5.5-acre campus of more than 20 fine art galleries, studios, and the City Garage theater. The Metro E Line's 26th St/Bergamot Station stop is immediately adjacent.

Day 3
From Hotel: 3 min · 2 min → Tongva Park
1. Tongva Park
A 6.2-acre park named for the Tongva people, opened in 2013 with undulating earthen berms, native and Mediterranean plantings, an amphitheater, and a dramatic overlook fountain — a striking modern counterpoint to Palisades Park's historic character next door.
Read more
Daily 6:00am - 11:00pm
~30 min
1615 Ocean Ave · Downtown Santa Monica
23 min · 3 min → Palisades Park
2. Palisades Park
A 26.4-acre bluff-top promenade above the Pacific, established in 1892 and designated a historic landmark in 2007. Features include the 1912 Idaho Gate, a Native American totem pole donated in 1926, a rose garden, and a restored Camera Obscura — with unbroken ocean views the length of the park.
Read more
Daily 6:00am - 8:00pm
~30 min
Ocean Ave · Santa Monica
22 min · 3 min → Annenberg Community Beach House
3. Annenberg Community Beach House
The last surviving piece of "Ocean House," the 1929 beach estate William Randolph Hearst built for Marion Davies, later the Sand & Sea Club before earthquake damage in 1994. The Annenberg Foundation restored the site in 2009 as a free public beach facility, preserving the historic pool house and grounds.

4 min → Will Rogers State Beach
4. Will Rogers State Beach
A long, relatively uncrowded state beach named for the humorist and actor whose 345-acre ranch once covered this stretch of coast — less commercial than Santa Monica's own beach, with a wide sand stretch below the Palisades bluffs.

37 min · 7 min → Getty Villa
5. Getty Villa
A reconstruction of the Villa dei Papiri, a 1st-century Roman country house buried by Vesuvius, built to house J. Paul Getty's antiquities collection. Cliffside gardens, a reflecting pool, and Mediterranean plantings surround galleries of Greek, Roman, and Etruscan art.

Local Tastes
Baja Fish Tacos
Battered or grilled white fish in corn tortillas with crema, shredded cabbage, and pico de gallo. A California coastal staple from the Baja tradition, found at casual spots along Main Street and near the pier.
Main Street · Santa Monica
Avocado Toast
A California breakfast staple built with local Haas avocados on seeded sourdough, finished with lemon, red pepper flakes, and sea salt. Found across cafes and bakeries citywide.
Huckleberry Bakery · 1014 Wilshire Blvd
In-N-Out Burger
The California chain founded in 1948. The Double-Double and Animal Style are the standard orders. The nearest location to the hotel is on Wilshire Boulevard.
In-N-Out Burger · 500 Wilshire Blvd

Packing for a Hike
Worth Knowing

The Marvin Braude Bike Trail runs 22 miles from Will Rogers State Beach north of the pier to Torrance Beach in the south — completely flat along the water. Starting at Santa Monica Pier and riding south to Venice takes about 30 minutes on a rental bike, passing Muscle Beach, the Venice Boardwalk, and the Venice Canals.

Bike rentals are available at the pier and along Ocean Front Walk.
